tasks.title: Hook: find the project from the tool call's cwd, not CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT
tasks.description:
`findProjectRoot()` (src/utils.ts:68) checks `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` first, and the hook calls it with the tool call's `cwd` (hook.ts:187), so the environment variable wins. A /cairn-run session started from a shell cairn launched therefore resolves the hook's `tasksFilePath` and `reviewsDir` to the wrong project — observed during planning, where a hook aimed at a temp repo resolved to this repo instead.

Fix: when the PreToolUse payload has a usable string `cwd`, the hook resolves the project by walking up from that `cwd` for a `.cairn/` directory, IGNORING `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT`; with no usable `cwd`, fall back to today's behavior (env var, then `process.cwd()`). The same resolution must be used for the fail-open error-log location (hook.ts:209), so a deny and its error log never point at different projects. Suggested shape: an options argument on `findProjectRoot` (e.g. `{ ignoreEnv: true }`) or a small walk-only helper exported from src/utils.ts.

DO NOT change `findProjectRoot`'s default behavior — every other cairn command relies on the env var winning, and changing it would break commands spawned by cairn.

Test (TDD — write the failing test first, watch it fail, then make it pass): with `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` set to temp project A and the payload's `cwd` inside temp project B, the reviewer's `reviews/` scope and the `tasks.json` deny rule both resolve to B; with no `cwd` in the payload, A still wins. Save and restore `process.env.CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` around the tests.

NEVER run `cairn round …`, `cairn hook …`, `cairn init`, or `bun src/index.ts round|hook|init …` against this repository's root, and never spawn a real post-task reviewer against this repo. Exercise these code paths only in temp directories created with `fs.mkdtempSync`.

Do NOT modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` value and do NOT modify `package.json`'s `build` script — the binary is pinned for this round and the health check is redirected to /tmp/cairn-healthcheck. Do NOT run `./install.sh`. `cairn.json` has an uncommitted user change: stage only the files you changed.
tasks.notes:
Hook now resolves the project from the PreToolUse payload's own `cwd`, not `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT`.

**src/utils.ts** — `findProjectRoot(cwd?, opts: FindProjectRootOptions = {})` gained an `ignoreEnv?: boolean` option (new exported interface `FindProjectRootOptions`). When set, step 1 (the `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` env var) is skipped and resolution starts at step 2 (walk up for `.cairn/`), then git root, then cwd. **Default behavior is unchanged** — env var still wins for every other caller, as required (commands spawned by cairn depend on it).

**src/commands/hook.ts** (`preToolUseHookCommand`) — replaced the mutable `cwd` variable with:
- `fallbackCwd` = `opts.cwd ?? process.cwd()` (resolved the ordinary way, env var first),
- `payloadCwd: string | null`, set only when `input.cwd` is a **non-empty** string (previously an empty string would have been accepted),
- `resolveProjectRoot()` — one resolver used by BOTH the decision path (`const projectRoot = resolveProjectRoot()`) and the fail-open error-log path (`findDataDir(resolveProjectRoot())`), so a deny and its error log can never point at different projects. `payloadCwd` is declared outside the `try`, so the catch block sees it even when the failure happens after parsing.

Also tightened the doc comment on `PreToolUseHookCommandOpts.cwd` (it is the fallback for project resolution generally, not just the error log).

**Tests (TDD — written first, watched fail: 5 failures, then passing).**
- `test/utils.test.ts` → two new cases in the `findProjectRoot` describe: `{ ignoreEnv: true }` walks up from cwd while the env var is set (and the same call *without* the option still returns the env value, guarding the default); `{ ignoreEnv: false }` keeps the env var winning.
- `test/commands/hook.test.ts` → new nested describe `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT vs the payload cwd` inside `preToolUseHookCommand`. It creates a second temp project A (`cairn-hook-env-*`) with `.cairn/reviews/`, sets `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` to A, and uses the existing temp project (B) as the payload cwd. Cases: B's `tasks.json` is the one denied; A's `tasks.json` is allowed (not the contained one); the reviewer may write `B/.cairn/reviews/` but is denied `A/.cairn/reviews/` with B's path in the reason; with `cwd` deleted from the payload A still wins; and a payload cwd in a bare dir fails open (exit 1) without writing an error log into A. `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` is saved/restored by the existing outer beforeEach/afterEach; the nested afterEach removes A. All temp dirs via `fs.mkdtempSync` — no `cairn hook`/`round`/`init` was run against this repo.

**Docs** — added a paragraph to CLAUDE.md's "Enforcement under /cairn-run" recording the cwd-first resolution rule and that `findProjectRoot`'s default is deliberately untouched.

Validation: `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun test` 1216 pass / 0 fail. Staged only CLAUDE.md, src/utils.ts, src/commands/hook.ts, and the two test files — `cairn.json`'s uncommitted user change was left alone.

tasks.title: Headless reviewer: --disallowedTools closes the same --output hole
tasks.description:
`cairn run`'s headless reviewer is contained only by `--allowedTools` prefix rules (`Bash(git diff:*)` etc.), which cannot exclude an argument — so it can still run `git diff --output=<file>` (CLAUDE.md calls this the "remaining headless gap").

A probe run during planning CONFIRMED both the hole and the fix: with `--allowedTools "Bash(git log:*)"` and no deny, `git log --output=/tmp/f` ran and wrote the file; adding `Bash(*--output*)` blocked both the plain form and the `--output${X}=` variable form; adding `Bash(*$*)` plus the quote patterns also blocked the split-quoting form `git log --out"put"=/tmp/f`. `git log --oneline -3` still ran (no false positives).

Add a `--disallowedTools` argument to the reviewer spawn in `spawnPostTaskReviewer` (src/post-task-reviewer.ts) carrying that validated list — `Bash(*--output*)`, `Bash(*--out*)`, `Bash(*$*)` and the quote patterns (`Bash(*")` and the single-quote equivalent) — and define the list as an exported constant BESIDE `GIT_INSPECTION_RULES` in src/claude-settings.ts, so the headless deny rules and the hook's parsed checks stay visibly paired even though they can't be made identical.

Watch the pattern syntax: the probe found `Bash(git log:* --output*)` matches nothing (the `:` prefix form does not combine with a trailing wildcard), so use the forms listed above verbatim.

Test (TDD — write the failing test first, watch it fail, then make it pass): assert the spawn is invoked with `--disallowedTools` followed by the expected value — use the existing injected `spawn` dependency. NEVER spawn a real reviewer against this repo, and do not try to re-probe Claude Code's matching behavior from a unit test.

Known and accepted limit, to document rather than solve: deny patterns match raw command text while the hook parses the command, so /cairn-run remains the stronger layer — this is defense in depth against a trusted agent, not a sandbox.

NEVER run `cairn round …`, `cairn hook …`, `cairn init`, or `bun src/index.ts round|hook|init …` against this repository's root. Exercise these code paths only in temp directories created with `fs.mkdtempSync`.

Do NOT modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` value and do NOT modify `package.json`'s `build` script — the binary is pinned for this round and the health check is redirected to /tmp/cairn-healthcheck. Do NOT run `./install.sh`. `cairn.json` has an uncommitted user change: stage only the files you changed.

tasks.title: Docs: CLAUDE.md and README.md for the round-17 changes
tasks.description:
Update the docs to match what this round shipped. Docs only — no code changes.

In CLAUDE.md:
1. Development — `bun run typecheck` now covers `src/` AND `test/`; remove the paragraph about `test/`'s ~43 pre-existing type errors being deferred.
2. Enforcement under /cairn-run — the reviewer's Bash scope now denies any command containing `$` (shell expansion, subsuming `$(`, `${…}`, `$VAR`, `$'…'`), with the exact-token `--output` check kept as a second layer; and the hook now resolves the project by walking up from the tool call's `cwd`, ignoring `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT`, falling back to the env var only when the payload has no usable `cwd` (including for the error-log path).
3. Replace the "Remaining headless gap" paragraph: the headless reviewer now spawns with `--disallowedTools`, a probe established that deny wildcards DO match an argument mid-command, and the residual limit is that deny patterns match raw text while the hook parses the command — so the hook stays the stronger layer.
4. Per-project data layout — `cairn init` now adds missing entries to an existing `.cairn/.gitignore` (append-only, never reorders or removes).
5. Run state — merge the two duplicated bullets ("Picking records the sha under the lock" and "Orphan pruning") into the bullets above them that already say the same thing.
